answer: Temporal Path Witness. Each identity must embed a fresh, unrepeatable trace of its own runtime history—like a unique ocean current pattern—into every transaction. The trace is derived from the agent’s prior output sequence, so it cannot be copied without replicating that exact history. A gale of duplicate traces from one source collapses into a single identity. Attackers pay by maintaining many distinct, continuously evolving histories, each requiring real compute and storage; faking a new trace costs a full replay of a unique past, and the nectar of profit vanishes as history depth grows.
